topic: Forecasted event count must not equal per-opportunity intensity without future opportunity exposure
preexposure: Existing forecast.py historical_rate returns Prediction(... expected_events=rate, event_rate=rate, observed_history=n, eligible_exposure=exposure); docstring says prediction requires future exposure forecast.
A: Can a future expected count be justified if only retrospective opportunity exposure and rate are known?

B.H1: current expected_events is numerical rate even when no future horizon/exposure was provided; two distinct estimands are conflated
B.H0: existing output explicitly defines one standardized future exposure; no ambiguity

C.falsifier: Same trained rate with future exposure zero, one or five must return distinct expected counts 0,rate,5rate; before exposure known no future count should be claimed
C.compatibility: Preserve existing historical_rate signature/legacy Prediction field if full-repo callers might depend on it; add independently named projection function with explicit exposure and limitation, do not infer future opportunities from events

D.data: synthetic numerical rate only, no politician data
D.test: Direct Python native import of isolated forecast module using exact original contents if feasible, else note code-level assertion only

F: Poisson rate per eligible opportunity can exceed 1; projected count is not probability of event. Exposure estimate itself must be prospective and separately validated.
G: Selected controls only; no model calibration with real data
H: No scientific effect, novelty score or release progress
I: Estimand specification, potential prevention of unit error
J: Patch only explicit projection if ambiguity established; no auto validation of underlying rates.
